name: alevatri/diorisisscan (Diorisis Scan beta 0.3, 9-2026) - greekScansions.json
licence: MIT License / Copyright (c) 2022 alevatri / 'Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in the Software without restriction...'
structure: JSON object: 577,570 keys (Beta Code word forms, e.g. '!a/bais') -> list of [syllable_index, mark] pairs (922,185 pairs in total); marks include the dash for long, a breve for short, plus overlong/resolved/anceps-type symbols. Only the syllables the scanner treats as needing a lookup are listed (not full per-word patterns).
derivation_statement: NONE found. The README (5,384 bytes) describes the scanner module only and never says how greekScansions.json was produced (no source corpus, no hand-marking claim, no dataset citation). The only code that writes the file is prosodyScanner.py manualScan(), which appends a form with a scansion typed in interactively by the user at the console to the dictionary. The repo name suggests a link to the Diorisis corpus but nothing states it.
decision: Survey only; NOT ingested (provenance not stated; the MIT licence covers the repository as a software licence and does not by itself establish rights in data of unknown origin). A scanner-generated dictionary is also not independent hand scansion.
see_also: If wanted later, ask the repository owner (alevatri) how the table was built (Diorisis corpus is CC BY 4.0 per Melos notes, figshare doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.6187256).
